description:
FILED s473t5d (Opus, 2026-09-13) by #1501 round 5 CHECK 2.

`tools/pclperl-for-tests` turns `-I DIR` into `-IDIR` on the `perl ... pl2cl`
command line -- so the TRANSPILER resolves modules there (that is #1284's half)
-- but the emitted program's own `@INC` never gains the directory, so a child
that INSPECTS `@INC` sees nothing:

  t/run/switchI.t rows 3+4:
    fresh_perl_is("print grep { \$_ eq 'Bla2' } \@INC[0..(\$#INC-1)]", 'Bla2',
                  { switches => ['-IBla2'], nolib => 1 }, '-I');
    PCL prints '' -- perl prints Bla2.

  t/run/switchM.t (all 5 rows): `-Irun/flib -Mfoo` must (a) find
  run/flib/foo.pmc in preference to foo.pm and (b) make a warning from inside
  the module name the file as `run/flib/foo.pmc`.  PCL produces neither.

FIX SHAPE: perl's `-I` does two things -- it prepends to `@INC` at compile time
AND it is visible to the program.  The prelude already carries the other
program-rewriting switches (`$/` for -0, `$\` for -l, `$^I` for -i since
#1700), so `unshift @INC, 'DIR';` belongs there, in the same block, in the
order perl uses (the LAST -I is searched first).

PROBE THE BREAKING CASE FIRST: every runperl child in the suite goes through
this wrapper, and test.pl's own `set_up_inc('../lib')` already manipulates
`@INC` -- so measure the whole companion population before and after, not just
switchI.t/switchM.t.  Note also that the real t/test.pl's `_create_runperl`
adds `"-I../lib" "-I."` unless `nolib`, and PCL's stub does not; switchI.t's
rows 3+4 pass `nolib => 1`, so they are the clean case to start from.

The `.pmc` half of switchM.t is a SECOND fact (perl prefers `foo.pmc` over
`foo.pm` when it is not older) and is independent of the @INC half; both of
run/switchM.t's `loads pmc` rows are additionally UNSTABLE against the blessed
snapshot -- measured 0/5 three times alone AND on a `git archive 2ff53f8d`
extraction, where the snapshot says 2/3, so that drift is PRE-EXISTING and
unattributed.
subject: `pclperl-for-tests -I DIR` reaches the TRANSPILE but not the child program's runtime @INC, so a child cannot see the directory it was given
